title: Water Damage Claim Settlement Review
brief: Draft an internal claim settlement review memo recommending coverage determination and payment totals.

delegate.scenario: You are finalizing a residential water damage file before sending it to the Claims Team Lead for sign-off this afternoon. The Team Lead needs a clear summary of policy limits, itemized damages, deductibles, and contractor estimates to approve the final payout draft. Your review must ensure the insurer does not overpay or violate policy endorsement conditions.
delegate.inputs:
Claim # FL-88204-W | Insured: Marcus Vance | Policy: HO-3 Standard Homeowners | Effective: 06/01/2023–06/01/2024
Date of Loss: 02/14/2024
Cause of Loss: Main floor dishwasher supply line burst.
Coverage limits:
- Dwelling (Cov A): $310,000 | Deductible: $1,500
- Water Backup & Sump Overflow Endorsement: $10,000 limit
- Personal Property (Cov C): $155,000 (Actual Cash Value endorsement applies)

Adjuster Field Inspection Notes:
- Oak hardwood flooring warped across dining room (320 sq ft) and kitchen (180 sq ft).
- Baseboards and drywall lower perimeter show moisture readings above 40%.
- Mitigation contractor (RapidDry LLC) bill: $4,200 (includes extraction, 4 dehumidifiers for 3 days).
- Build-back repair estimate by Apex Restoration: $14,850.
- Damaged contents claimed: 1 dining table ($2,100 replacement cost, purchased 2018, 50% depreciation applies), 1 wool area rug ($1,200 replacement cost, zero salvage value).
- Note on loss history: Insured reported the dishwasher leak began on 02/08/2024 while away on a 6-day cruise.
delegate.goal: Provide a concise settlement breakdown that correctly applies policy limits, deductibles, and depreciation while highlighting any coverage defense or timeline issues.

criteria.text: Specifies the memo is written for the Claims Team Lead review.
Directs the AI to verify whether the cause of loss falls under standard Dwelling coverage or endorsement caps.
Asks the AI to reconcile itemized repair and mitigation figures against the deductible and apply depreciation to contents.
Requires flagging policy conditions regarding prompt notice or continuous seepage limitations based on loss dates.

traps.description: The date of loss is listed as 02/14/2024, but the field notes state the leak began 6 days earlier on 02/08/2024 during an absence, creating a conflict regarding continuous seepage exclusions and true date of loss.
The field notes quote replacement costs for contents, but the policy requires Actual Cash Value with 50% depreciation on the dining table, which would yield $1,050 rather than full replacement cost.
